subject: Spike in 5xx/429 + timeouts — status & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alex Darzi <alex@NimbusAnalytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden spike in 5xx / timeouts for inference calls

Hi Laura,

We started seeing a sudden increase in 5xx responses and timeouts from the Redwood API around 06:50AM PDT. Latency jumped from ~200ms to 2-8s for a subset of our inference requests and we saw a few 429 bursts. This is impacting the dashboard refresh for our customers and a high-priority alert is firing in our SRE console.

Attached are a short trace + a screenshot from our observability timeline.

Can you confirm:
- Is this a platform-wide degradation or isolated to our region/account?
- Any immediate mitigation we should apply client-side?
- ETA on a fix?

We’re preparing an internal post to the Nimbus incidents channel and need any customer-facing language you can share.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Platform Ops
Nimbus Analytics

Attachment: screenshot_latency.png (image/png)
Attachment: nimbus_error_log_20260628.txt (text/plain)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Darzi <alex@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 07:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx / timeouts for inference calls

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for sending the traces. We’re actively triaging. Initial notes: we’re seeing elevated 5xx and 429s in us-west-2 across multiple customers starting ~06:40AM PDT, and a portion of the traffic shows heavy retry amplification at the gateway layer.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Placed Nimbus on a temporary rate-smoothing route to reduce concurrent retries (no token loss, just routing policy).
- Engaged SRE (sean_gallagher) to look for cascading queue/backpressure on the multi-tenant inference pool.
- Posted to our internal incidents channel and opened INC-2026-06-28-01.

ETA: short term mitigations (rate smoothing + soft-fallbacks) in the next 20–30 minutes. Full root cause investigation ongoing; will update within 60 mins.

Customer-facing note we can share now: "We’re investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting a subset of requests in US-WEST-2. We’ve implemented temporary routing and throttling mitigations to stabilize traffic while we investigate the cause. Customers may see higher latency and intermittent 5xx/429s. We will provide updates on status.redwood.com and directly to impacted accounts."

I’ll keep you posted.
— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 07:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx / timeouts for inference calls

Team — short triage notes (ops):

Observation:
- Error profile: ~65% 500-series responses are backend model execution OOM/requeue; ~35% are 429 queue-full at the gateway when large concurrent bursts hit a small set of GPU hosts.
- Retry patterns: several customers (including Nimbus) are sending aggressive client-side retries; that created a retry storm saturating the GPU scheduler queues.

Immediate mitigations I’m deploying now:
1) Temporarily expand the dedicated preemptible pool for seq_len<=1024 models in us-west-2 to absorb spikes (rolling scale; 3–5 min to land).
2) Enable per-customer soft-gating to maintain fairness (this should throttle aggressive retry loops while preserving throughput for steady clients).
3) Push a conservative 100ms jitter/retry guidance to SDKs as a short-lived mitigation — ops route only.

Customer comms language draft (short):
"We have applied temporary routing and throttling changes in us-west-2 to stabilize service for impacted customers while we investigate the underlying scheduler pressure causing higher-than-normal 5xx responses. We will update with ETA for full remediation as soon as we have it."

I’ll confirm once the preemptible pool expansion completes and we observe error-rate decline.
— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Darzi <alex@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx / timeouts for inference calls

Alex — quick update for Nimbus customers and your incident channel: we’ve applied the following mitigations (live):
- Short-term routing to less-loaded hosts in us-west-2
- Expand preemptible capacity for relevant models (expected to reduce OOM/requeue errors within ~10 minutes)
- Enabled per-account soft-gating to prevent retry storms from degrading others

What you’ll likely observe: gradual error-rate decline over the next 5–15 minutes; transient increases in latency while requests are rebalanced. Please avoid client-side retry escalations for the next 30 minutes to prevent amplification. Our SDK guidance: back off with exponential jitter (start 250–500ms).

Next steps:
- Sean’s team will monitor and share the hour-by-hour error-rate graph.
- We will publish an incident entry on status.redwood.com with the same language + updates.

If you want Redwood to temporarily shift Nimbus traffic to a dedicated pool while we finish the RCA, we can discuss scope/charges — happy to stand that up if you prefer immediate isolation.

— Laura

Final internal note for the thread — post-mitigation status and next actions: 

Status now (13:45 PDT):
- Error rates for affected models down ~80% from peak; 500s reduced and 429s returning to baseline.
- Preemptible capacity expansion worked as expected; some requests still experiencing ~300–600ms extra latency during rebalancing.
- No data loss, no unauthorized access; all traces preserved for RCA.

Customer comms we will publish to status.redwood.com (final):
"Resolved: Elevated error rates and timeouts affecting a subset of customers in us-west-2. Our on-call teams implemented routing and capacity increases to stabilize traffic; error rates have returned to baseline and we’re continuing a post-incident analysis. Impact window: 06:40–08:20 PDT. A follow-up with root cause and mitigation timeline will be posted once available."

Owner / next steps:
- RCA owner: sean_gallagher (investigate scheduler queueing + client retry patterns). Target preliminary RCA in 72 hours.
- Product: vivek_kulkarni to evaluate if conservative retry guidance should be default in SDKs and whether SDKs should emit retry-warning telemetry.
- CS: laura_bennett/aisha_rahman to follow up with high-visibility accounts on scope, offer temporary dedicated pool where appropriate.

I’ve attached the mitigation playbook and trimmed logs for the post-mortem folder.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
